title: Lisse sheaves and continuous representations
statement:
Let $Y$ be a connected scheme with a geometric point $\bar y$, and let $\pi_1=\pi_1(Y,\bar y)$ be the profinite group of [def-galois-fibre-functor]; stalks at $\bar y$ are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].

1. *(Finite coefficients.)* Let $\Lambda$ be a finite ring. Evaluation at $\bar y$, $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F_{\bar y}$, with $\sigma\in\pi_1$ acting on $\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ as the natural automorphism $\sigma$ of the fibre functor on the underlying finite locally constant sheaf of sets [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves], is an exact equivalence between the category of locally constant sheaves of finite left $\Lambda$-modules on $Y_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] (sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules etale locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finite $\Lambda$-module), with $\Lambda$-linear maps, and the category of finite left $\Lambda$-modules with a continuous $\Lambda$-linear action of $\pi_1$ (discrete topology), with equivariant $\Lambda$-linear maps. These sheaves form a full abelian subcategory of all sheaves of $\Lambda$-modules, closed under kernels and cokernels. It is a tensor equivalence: for commutative $\Lambda$ it carries $\mathcal F\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G$ to $\mathcal F_{\bar y}\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal G_{\bar y}$ with the diagonal action, compatibly with the associativity, commutativity and unit constraints, and the constant sheaf $\underline\Lambda$ to the trivial representation $\Lambda$. It is compatible with base change along a homomorphism $\Lambda\to\Lambda'$ of finite rings: it carries $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F$ to $\Lambda'\otimes_\Lambda\mathcal F_{\bar y}$ with the action $1\otimes\sigma$, naturally in $\mathcal F$ and compatibly with composites $\Lambda\to\Lambda'\to\Lambda''$.
2. *($\ell$-adic coefficients.)* Assume moreover that $Y$ is Noetherian and separated and that $\ell$ is invertible on $Y$. Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Qlb$ an algebraic closure of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $E\subset\Qlb$ a finite extension of $\mathbf Q_\ell$. With the lisse $\mathcal O_E$-, $E$- and $\Qlb$-sheaves on $Y$ and their fibres at $\bar y$ of [def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves], and the representations of [def-pod-l-adic-representations], the fibre at $\bar y$ with $\pi_1$ acting through (1) at every finite level is an equivalence from lisse $\mathcal O_E$-sheaves to continuous $\mathcal O_E$-representations of $\pi_1$, from lisse $E$-sheaves to continuous $E$-representations of $\pi_1$, and from lisse $\Qlb$-sheaves to $\ell$-adic representations of $\pi_1$ on finite-dimensional $\Qlb$-vector spaces. At the levels $E$ and $\Qlb$ both categories are abelian and the equivalence is exact. At every level it carries tensor products to tensor products with the diagonal action and the unit sheaf to the trivial representation, and it commutes with scalar extension along $E\subset L$ in $\Qlb$.

proof.text: Use the proved exists_fiber_flc_equivalence to obtain Φ, E, γ, their Yoneda comparison and the normalized finite-set fibre comparison. Compose its inverse with the comparison Φ ⋙ E to the finite-etale action equivalence to construct η. Naturality of the comparison gives the finite-etale action identity.

Transfer finite limits to FLC through Φ. The finite-etale inclusion preserves finite limits by change of morphism property, and uliftYoneda preserves them, so the Yoneda comparison makes the FLC sheaf inclusion preserve finite limits. Construct the finite-carrier equivalence by module ULift: it is fully faithful, and every finite large representation is the lift of its Shrink with transported operations. Its action comparison is the counit of Rep.repIsoAction. Construct the equivalence from ambient-product LambdaModuleObject to InternalModule in FLC by pulling its operations back through the product-preserving full inclusion. Derive the generalized-element axioms from the ambient diagrams. Conversely map internal operations to ambient sheaves using inverse product and terminal comparisons and derive all ten diagrams from the generalized-element axioms. The operation compatibility equations identify the morphisms; the reverse construction is an exact preimage, proving essential surjectivity. Construct κ by the forgetful-functor filtered-colimit comparison and prove its equality on every section germ. Apply new-e4-galois-finite-module-lift with these proved interfaces to obtain the module equivalences, linear stalk comparison and normalized evaluation action. Form the finite data record.

Identify the source lisse-module predicate with the finite locally constant module-sheaf predicate. Transport closure under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels; obtain zero and binary products from the zero sheaf and finite biproducts. Mathlib Abelian.Subcategory gives the abelian category. The finite equivalences preserve finite limits and colimits automatically.

For any finite constant module, its module stalk is the constant value. The underlying constant zero module has singleton stalk. For each constant value a, the underlying set map from that zero module to the constant module sending every section to the constant section a is a map in FLC. Naturality of every fibre automorphism and the singleton stalk fix its image, which is the germ of a. Thus evaluation on the constant coefficient module is trivial. The normalized stalk comparison gives its representation isomorphism with the trivial module.

Constants and tensor products are lisse, so the full lisse subcategory inherits its monoidal and braided structures and a braided sheaf inclusion. Construct B by restricting actual sheafified ring extension of scalars, using lisse_ring_scalar_extension; its underlying-sheaf comparison is the identity. Construct the natural comparison for composite sheaf scalar extensions by inverting the sheafification of the first unit after the second extension and composing with the sheafified module associator. The second extension preserves sheafification because it is a left adjoint. Naturality of the sheafification unit, together with the module adjunction units, proves that the comparison sends b tensor (a tensor z) to b g(a) tensor z on sections. Lift it through the full lisse inclusion. Construct the scalar-stalk comparison at the unlifted geometric point from the filtered-colimit comparison for the scalar-extension left adjoint and the point invariance of sheafification. Naturality of the sheafification unit proves that this natural isomorphism sends a tensor germ(z) to the germ of the sheafified a tensor z. Apply new-e4-galois-finite-tensor-scalar to supply the braided representation functor and the actual scalar comparisons. Assemble all fields of GaloisLisseFiniteCorrespondence.

The fundamental-group homeomorphism identifies G with the automorphisms of the finite-etale fibre, so it is Hausdorff and totally disconnected. With its given compact group structure, take ProfiniteGrp.of G and the identity continuous group isomorphism δ. For each allowed prime and algebraic closure, apply new-e4-galois-adic-from-finite to this supplied model and the assembled finite correspondence. This gives the required adic correspondence with its same evaluation automorphism.

split_report.summary: The finite-coefficient part now follows Stacks Lemma 0DV5 (and Milne LEC Prop. 6.16, p. 49): the blueprint's first step ('thm-galois-lc-etale applied to the underlying sheaf of sets together with the module structure') hid two arguments, now nodes: lisse Lambda-module sheaves are Lambda-module objects in FLC(Y) (lem-pod-lisse-module-sheaves-as-module-objects) and a finite-product-preserving equivalence induces an equivalence of module objects, module objects in finite pi_1-sets being finite Lambda[pi_1]-modules (lem-pod-equivalence-induces-module-objects). Exactness now uses the existing closed node lemma-constructible-flc-serre and prop-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks-exact instead of re-deriving it; the tensor and base-change steps (elementary: null before) now use the new lem-pod-lisse-tensor-and-scalar-extension (Stacks 093V/095D, 03EL) for local constancy and the stalk formulas. The Qlbar clause was not provable as stated: it cited 'the coefficient conventions of def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes', which defines lisse sheaves only for finite commutative rings and has no Qlbar conventions, spoke of 'finite stalks' for Qlbar-sheaves, and its proof ('filtered colimit of finite-level ones') does not match how l-adic sheaves are built (limits over levels, then isogeny, then colimit over E). The statement is rewritten into part (2) with explicit categories: new definitions def-pod-lisse-l-adic-sheaves (Weil II (1.1.1) b-d restricted to lisse objects) and def-pod-l-adic-representations (Weil II (1.1.6)); the proof goes O_E -> E -> Qlbar following the sketch of Stanford Weil II seminar L19 Prop. 1.1.9, with new nodes lem-pod-adic-limit-finite-modules (Stacks 09B8, 031D, 00MA) and lem-pod-profinite-stable-lattice (L19, pp. 2-3). def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes dropped from stmt_deps and proof (not used); stmt_deps now name the fundamental group, stalks, locally constant sheaves, the etale site and the two new definitions.

lean.statement: theorem galois_lisse_representations {Y : Scheme.{u}} [ConnectedSpace Y] {Ω : Type u} [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ Y) (G : Type u) [Group G] [TopologicalSpace G] [IsTopologicalGroup G] [CompactSpace G] [∀ P, MulAction G ((FiniteEtale.fiber y).obj P)] [IsFundamentalGroup (FiniteEtale.fiber y) G] : ∃ c : GaloisLisseFiniteCorrespondence y G, ∀ (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] [IsNoetherian Y] [Y.IsSeparated] [∀ x : Y, Invertible (l : Y.residueField x)] (Q : Type (u + 1)) [Field Q] [Algebra ℚ_[l] Q] [IsAlgClosure ℚ_[l] Q], Nonempty (GaloisLisseAdicCorrespondence y G c l Q)

statement_change.what: Only part (2) omitted the Noetherian, separated and ell-invertible assumptions of Weil II (0.1) needed to type its lisse-adic sheaves. Spec F_ell satisfies the original preamble but ell is not invertible. Adding those assumptions to the preamble would incorrectly restrict part (1), contrary to Stacks 0DV5. They are added only at the start of part (2).

source.place: Weil II (0.1), p. 144; (1.1.1) b)-d), pp. 146-147; finite part unchanged as in Stacks 0DV5 (3)

citers.note: Its geometric scheme is separated of finite type over the fixed algebraically closed finite-field base, with ell different from the characteristic by the standing coefficient convention.
It inherits the separated finite-type and prime-to-characteristic setting of def-wf-fundamental-representation.

The finite-coefficient uses remain valid, as do the separated finite-type Weil and curve cases; the general adic assertion in (3) does not assume V separated or ell invertible and cannot use the corrected adic clause in those cases.
The curve and its finite-field base changes are separated and Noetherian, with ell different from the characteristic in the standing coefficient convention.
It uses only finite coefficients on an arbitrary connected scheme, so part (1) is unchanged and applies without adic assumptions.
